chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man buys two sisters, so he sleeps with one of them, then he sleeps with the other out of ignorance.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he sleeps with the other one out of ignorance, the first one does not become prohibited to him, but if he sleeps with the other one while knowing that she is prohibited to him, both together become prohibited to him.'

key_terms.يَطَأُ: he sleeps with / consummates marriage with

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping with the second sister while married to the first automatically prohibit both sisters if the man was unaware of the rule?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of *jam' al-ukhtayn* by distinguishing between *jahala* (ignorance) and *'ilm* (knowledge) as the determining factors for permanent prohibition. It establishes that if a man unknowingly consummates the marriage with the second sister while the first is still valid, the first remains permissible; however, if he knowingly does so, both become permanently prohibited to him. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intentionality and awareness of the individual in determining legal consequences within family law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man buys the two sisters, so he sleeps with one of the two. Then he sleeps with the other out of ignorance’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he slept with the other one out of ignorance, the first one would not be Prohibited unto him, but if he slept with the other one and he knew that she is prohibited unto him, they would both together be Prohibited unto him’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys two sisters and goes to bed with one of them, then goes to bed with the other due to ignorance. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has gone to bed with the other due to ignorance the first one does not become unlawful for him but if he goes to bed with the other knowing that it is unlawful, both of them become unlawful for him.’”
